question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

His father was killed in a ______, when the boy was nine years old.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. duel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "duel" is a prearranged fight between two people with weapons (swords or pistols), fought according to fixed rules to settle a point of honour. (द्वंद्वयुद्ध)

◦ Correct: His father was killed in a duel, when the boy was nine years old.

• Only a fight can "kill" someone, so the noun required here is duel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dwell" is a verb meaning to live/reside somewhere; it cannot follow the article "a".

• Option 2 "drool" means to let saliva fall from the mouth — meaningless here.

• Option 3 "dual" is an adjective meaning double/having two parts (dual citizenship, dual control); an adjective cannot be the object of "in a ______".

NOTE

• Beware the classic homophone pair: duel (a fight — noun) vs dual (double — adjective). Similar SSC pairs: council/counsel, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, complement/compliment.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

Something that is necessary or crucial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Indispensable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indispensable" means absolutely necessary; essential; something that cannot be done without. (अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य)

◦ Example: Water is indispensable to life.

• The prefix "in-" (not) + "dispensable" (that can be done away with) literally gives "that cannot be dispensed with".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pedantic" — excessively concerned with minor rules and bookish details.

• Option 2 "Trivial" — of little value or importance; this is the opposite of the required meaning.

• Option 4 "Auxiliary" — giving additional or supporting help; extra, not essential.

NOTE

• Synonyms of indispensable: essential, vital, crucial, imperative, requisite. Antonyms: dispensable, unnecessary, superfluous, trivial.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Each band is known across a wide area because all residents of a given region are typically tied to one another through a large ______ of kinship and reciprocity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. network.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "network" means a large interconnected system/group of people or things linked to one another. People "tied to one another" through kinship (family ties) and reciprocity (mutual give-and-take) form a network of relationships. (जाल / संजाल)

◦ Correct: ... all residents ... are typically tied to one another through a large network of kinship and reciprocity.

• The collocation "a network of" (a network of roads, a network of friends, a social network) is the standard English expression here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "variation" (a change or difference in condition) does not describe ties between people.

• Option 2 "mesh" refers literally to netting/woven material; "a mesh of kinship" is not idiomatic English.

• Option 4 "clash" (a conflict or violent confrontation) contradicts "tied to one another", which is positive.

NOTE

• Useful collocations for SSC: a network of relations, a chain of events, a web of lies, a circle of friends, a flock of birds.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'

The police released a statement saying/, "This was one of the most vicious/ attack we have ever seen."
option_2: The police released a statement saying,
option_3: "This was one of the most vicious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. attack we have ever seen."

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" always takes a plural noun. So "one of the most vicious attacks", not "attack".

◦ Correct: The police released a statement saying, "This was one of the most vicious attacks we have ever seen."

• "One of ..." implies selecting one item out of a group, and a group must be plural.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The police released a statement saying," is correct — "police" is a plural collective noun and takes a plural verb, and "released" is correctly in the past tense.

• '"This was one of the most vicious' is correct — "most vicious" is the proper superlative of the long adjective "vicious".

• Since a definite error exists, "No error" (Option 1) is wrong.

NOTE

• Remember the pattern: One of the + superlative + plural noun + singular verb — "One of the tallest buildings in the city is ...". Only the verb is singular; the noun after "one of the" must be plural.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

Social justice has been one of the cherished goals of the makers of our Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. despised.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cherished" means held dear; deeply loved, valued and protected. (संजोया हुआ / प्रिय)

• Its antonym is "despised", meaning hated, looked down upon with contempt. (घृणा करना)

◦ Example: He cherished his mother's letters, but despised the man who wrote against her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "relished" (enjoyed greatly) is close in sense to cherished — not an antonym.

• Option 2 "valued" (regarded as important) is a synonym of cherished.

• Option 3 "treasured" (kept as precious) is also a synonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of cherish: treasure, value, prize, adore, hold dear, nurture. Antonyms: despise, loathe, abhor, detest, scorn, disdain.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

This looks (like one of those unwelcome social summons which call upon a man) either to be bored or to lie.
option_1: like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man
option_2: like one of these unwelcome social summons that call upon a man
option_3: like one of those unwelcome social summon that call upon a man
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "one of those", the noun must be in the plural. The plural of the noun "summons" is "summonses" (summons – summonses), exactly like bus – buses, gas – gases.

◦ Correct: This looks like one of those unwelcome social summonses which call upon a man either to be bored or to lie.

• The relative pronoun "which" correctly refers back to the plural noun "summonses", and the plural verb "call" agrees with it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 uses "these", which points to something near/at hand and clashes with the general, distant reference required here; it also keeps the wrong singular "summons".

• Option 3 uses "summon", which is a verb (to call/order someone to come), not the plural noun.

• Option 4 "No substitution required" is wrong because the singular "summons" after "one of those" is a clear grammatical error.

NOTE

• "Summons" (noun) = an official order to appear, especially in a court of law; plural summonses. "Summon" (verb) = to call someone to come or to order someone's presence. Nouns ending in -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -z form the plural by adding -es.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

When I was eight years old, I used to played with toys.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. used to play.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "used to + V1 (base form)" expresses a past habit or a repeated action that no longer happens. Hence "used to play", never "used to played".

◦ Correct: When I was eight years old, I used to play with toys.

• The time reference "When I was eight years old" clearly signals a discontinued past habit — the perfect context for "used to".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "used to played" (to + V2) is ungrammatical.

• Option 2 "use to played" is doubly wrong — wrong tense form of "use" and wrong verb form after it.

• Option 3 "used to playing" would be right only in the different structure "be/get used to + V-ing" (= be accustomed to), e.g., "I am used to playing".

NOTE

• Distinguish carefully:

◦ used to + V1 = past habit ("I used to smoke").

◦ be used to + V-ing/noun = be accustomed to ("I am used to smoking / to the noise").

◦ get used to + V-ing = become accustomed to.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Wage
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Emolument.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wage" (noun) means the money paid to a worker, usually for work done on an hourly, daily or weekly basis. (मज़दूरी / वेतन)

• "Emolument" means the salary, fee or profit received from employment or an office — the closest synonym. (उपलब्धि / पारिश्रमिक)

◦ Example: The judges' emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sycophant" — a flatterer who praises powerful people for personal gain. (चापलूस)

• Option 2 "Jocular" — fond of joking, humorous. (विनोदी)

• Option 4 "Jackpot" — a large cash prize won in a game or lottery, not regular earned pay.

NOTE

• Synonyms of wage: salary, pay, earnings, remuneration, stipend, emolument, honorarium. Note also that "wage" as a verb means to carry on (a war/campaign) — "to wage war".

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

There is no need to panic, not yet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fright.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Panic" means sudden uncontrollable fear or alarm that prevents clear thinking. (घबराहट / आतंक)

• "Fright" means sudden intense fear — the closest synonym among the options. (भय / डर)

◦ Example: The crowd was seized with panic/fright when the fire alarm rang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mock" — to make fun of, to ridicule.

• Option 2 "cheer" — to shout in joy or encouragement; this is the opposite in feeling.

• Option 4 "block" — to obstruct or stop something.

NOTE

• Synonyms of panic: fright, terror, alarm, dread, hysteria, consternation. Antonyms: calm, composure, serenity, confidence. Related idiom: "to press the panic button" = to react in a hurried, alarmed way.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Monitour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Monitour" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Monitor" — a person or device that watches, checks or keeps track of something (also the display screen of a computer). (निगरानी करना / मॉनिटर)

◦ Spelling key: MO + NI + TOR (it ends in -tor, like actor, doctor, editor, inspector — not in "-tour").

◦ Correct: The nurse will monitor the patient's temperature every hour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Slope" (a surface with one end higher than the other), "Constant" (unchanging; continuous) and "Chemical" (relating to chemistry / a substance) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Agent nouns from Latin usually end in -or: monitor, doctor, actor, sailor, governor, inspector, supervisor. Do not confuse with "tour" (a journey), which is a different word altogether.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Potato milk is ______ another option for those wanting an alternative to cow's milk.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. yet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "yet" is used as an adverb of emphasis before "another", giving the sense of "still one more / in addition to the ones already existing".

◦ Correct: Potato milk is yet another option for those wanting an alternative to cow's milk.

• "Yet another" is a fixed, idiomatic collocation meaning "one more of the same kind, added to many".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "though" and Option 4 "but" are contrast conjunctions; there is no contrast in this sentence, and neither can stand between "is" and "another".

• Option 3 "so" shows result/consequence, which the sentence does not express.

NOTE

• Other emphatic uses of "yet": "yet again" (once more), "yet more" (still more), "as yet" (up to now), "yet to come" (still in the future).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To make one's mouth water
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Feel hungry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to make one's mouth water" means to make someone feel hungry / to create a strong desire for food by its sight or smell (because the mouth literally produces saliva). (मुँह में पानी आना)

◦ Example: The smell of hot samosas made my mouth water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To make faces" = to twist one's face into funny or rude expressions.

• Option 2 "To tremble with fear" corresponds to idioms like "to have one's heart in one's mouth" or "to shake like a leaf".

• Option 3 "To feel no pain" is unrelated to appetite.

NOTE

• Related food idioms: "mouth-watering" (delicious-looking), "eat like a horse" (eat a lot), "a piece of cake" (very easy), "bread and butter" (a means of livelihood).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Misunderstand
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Comprehend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Misunderstand" means to fail to understand correctly; to interpret wrongly. (गलत समझना)

• Its antonym is "comprehend", meaning to grasp or understand fully. (समझना)

◦ Example: She did not misunderstand him; she comprehended his point perfectly.

• The prefix "mis-" means wrongly/badly: mis + understand = understand wrongly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Impossible" (not able to happen) is unrelated to understanding.

• Option 3 "Delayed" (postponed, late) refers to time, not comprehension.

• Option 4 "Sluggish" (slow-moving, lacking energy) refers to speed/energy.

NOTE

• Words with the prefix mis- (wrongly): misjudge, misinterpret, mislead, misplace, misuse, misbehave. Synonyms of comprehend: understand, grasp, perceive, fathom, discern.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A sound that cannot be heard
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Inaudible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inaudible" means that cannot be heard (too faint for the ear to catch). (अश्रव्य)

◦ Formation: in- (not) + audible (able to be heard, from Latin "audire" = to hear).

◦ Example: His reply was almost inaudible over the noise of the traffic.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Audacious" — daring, bold, showing a willingness to take risks.

• Option 3 "Autonomous" — self-governing, independent.

• Option 4 "Delible" — that can be erased or rubbed out (its opposite, "indelible", means permanent).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes for SSC: invisible (that cannot be seen), illegible (that cannot be read), incorrigible (that cannot be corrected), inevitable (that cannot be avoided), edible (fit to be eaten), indelible (that cannot be erased).

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: And he wanted to sea him sufer.
option_2: And he wanted to see him sufer.
option_3: And he wanted to see him suffer.
option_4: And he wantted to see him suffer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. And he wanted to see him suffer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three words are correctly spelt only in Option 3:

◦ "wanted" — WANT + ED (single "t"),

◦ "see" — to perceive with the eyes,

◦ "suffer" — to undergo pain or hardship, spelt with a double "f" (SUF + FER).

◦ Correct: And he wanted to see him suffer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has two errors — "sea" (a large body of salt water, a homophone of "see") and "sufer" (missing an "f").

• Option 2 misspells "suffer" as "sufer".

• Option 4 misspells "wanted" as "wantted" (the final "t" is not doubled because the stress and vowel pattern do not require it).

NOTE

• Doubling rule: a final consonant is doubled before -ed/-ing only in a stressed syllable with a single short vowel — stop → stopped, plan → planned. "Want" ends in -nt (two consonants), so it stays single: wanted.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

After the concert, his voice has hoarse from cheering.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. voice was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hoarse" is an adjective (rough and harsh in sound), so it needs a linking verb (be), not the auxiliary "has". Since the event is over — "After the concert" — the simple past "was" is required.

◦ Correct: After the concert, his voice was hoarse from cheering.

• "voice" is a singular subject, so the singular past form "was" agrees with it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No improvement" is wrong because "his voice has hoarse" has no main verb linking the adjective.

• Option 3 "voiced was" wrongly turns the noun "voice" into a verb, leaving the sentence without a subject.

• Option 4 "voice were" breaks subject–verb agreement — a singular subject cannot take "were".

NOTE

• Note the homophones: hoarse (rough-voiced) and horse (the animal). Linking verbs (be, seem, appear, become, feel, look, sound) are followed by adjectives, not adverbs — "His voice was hoarse", "She looks tired".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Why is your friend giving me weird looks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is completely correct, so "No error" is the right choice.

◦ "Why is your friend" — correct interrogative word order: question word (Why) + auxiliary (is) + subject (your friend).

◦ "giving me" — correct present-continuous form ("is giving") with the indirect object "me".

◦ "weird looks?" — "weird" (strange, odd) is correctly spelt and correctly modifies the plural noun "looks"; the question mark is properly placed.

• Full sentence: Why is your friend giving me weird looks?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The present continuous ("is giving") is appropriate because the action is happening at the moment of speaking.

• "Give someone a look / looks" is a standard collocation meaning to look at someone in a particular way.

NOTE

• Spelling tip: "weird" is a famous exception to the "i before e except after c" rule — remember "we are weird". Question-formation rule: Wh-word + auxiliary + subject + main verb.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

She had no ______ of telling him the truth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. intention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the determiner "no", a noun is needed, and the correct noun form is "intention" (a plan or aim to do something). (इरादा / मंशा)

◦ Correct: She had no intention of telling him the truth.

• The fixed structure is "to have no intention of + V-ing" — note the preposition "of" followed by the gerund "telling".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "intending" is a present participle/gerund, not the noun required after "no".

• Option 2 "intended" is a past participle/adjective ("the intended result").

• Option 3 "intents" is used only in the fixed legal phrase "to all intents and purposes"; "no intents of" is not idiomatic.

NOTE

• Word family: intend (verb), intention (noun), intentional (adjective), intentionally (adverb). Compare structures: "intend to do" but "have no intention of doing".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Soap removes traces of pesticides and heavy metals that hand sanitizers can left behind.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sanitizers can left behind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After a modal verb such as "can", the verb must be in its base form (V1). Hence it should be "can leave behind", not "can left behind".

◦ Correct: Soap removes traces of pesticides and heavy metals that hand sanitizers can leave behind.

• "left" is the past/past-participle form (leave – left – left) and cannot follow "can".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Soap removes traces of pesticides" is correct — "soap" is an uncountable singular subject taking the singular verb "removes".

• "and heavy metals that hand" is correct — the relative pronoun "that" properly introduces the clause describing the traces.

• As a clear error exists, "No error" (Option 4) is wrong.

NOTE

• Modals (can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must) are always followed by the bare infinitive (V1): "He can swim", "She must go", "They should have gone" (have + V3, never "must went").

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To turn over a new leaf
option_1: To have an inclination towards gardening
option_3: To turn your back on someone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To make a fresh start.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to turn over a new leaf" means to change one's behaviour for the better; to make a completely fresh start. Here "leaf" means a page of a book — turning it over begins a clean, blank page. (नया जीवन शुरू करना / सुधर जाना)

◦ Example: After his release from jail, he decided to turn over a new leaf and start an honest business.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 takes "leaf" literally as a plant leaf — a trap answer.

• Option 3 "To turn your back on someone" is a different idiom meaning to abandon or refuse to help someone.

• Option 4 "To reply brazenly" corresponds to "to answer back" or "to be barefaced", not to this idiom.

NOTE

• Related idioms of change and beginning: "start afresh / from scratch", "wipe the slate clean", "a clean slate", "mend one's ways".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Royal Canadian Mint" is the name of a unique, one-of-its-kind institution, and names of such specific bodies take the definite article "the".

◦ Correct: ... (1) the Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin ...

• Rule: "the" is used before the names of organisations, departments, and institutions of the pattern "the + Adjective + Noun" (the Reserve Bank of India, the United Nations, the Supreme Court).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a" is the indefinite article used for a non-specific, first-mentioned singular countable noun — wrong for a unique named institution.

• Options 2 "in" and 3 "of" are prepositions; the blank is followed by a noun phrase acting as the subject of "unveiled", so a preposition cannot fit.

NOTE

• "The" is used with: unique objects (the sun, the moon), rivers/oceans/mountain ranges (the Ganga, the Himalayas), newspapers (the Hindu), organisations (the WHO), and superlatives (the best).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "on" is used before the days of the week and before specific dates. The blank is followed by "Monday", so "on Monday" is required.

◦ Correct: ... unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) on Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "at" is used for exact points of clock time and for specific places (at 5 o'clock, at night, at the door) — not with days.

• Option 2 "through" indicates movement from one end to another or duration ("through the tunnel", "Monday through Friday").

• Option 4 "over" means above or across, or during an extended period ("over the weekend") — not with a single named day.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time: at + clock time (at 6 pm, at noon, at night); on + days/dates (on Monday, on 15 August); in + months/years/seasons/parts of the day (in July, in 2023, in winter, in the morning).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. an.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by "undergraduate", which begins with the vowel sound /ʌ/. Before a vowel sound, the indefinite article "an" is used.

◦ Correct: Fox was (3) an undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU ...

• Also, this is the first mention of Fox's status, so an indefinite article (a/an) is right, not "the".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "their" is a plural possessive and cannot refer to the singular "Fox".

• Option 2 "a" is used only before a consonant sound; "a undergraduate" is wrong.

• Option 4 "the" would wrongly suggest a particular, already-known student.

NOTE

• The a/an choice depends on sound, not spelling: an hour, an honest man, an MP, an X-ray (vowel sounds) vs a university, a European, a one-rupee coin, a useful book (consonant /j/ and /w/ sounds).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. amputation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amputation" means the surgical removal (cutting off) of a limb or part of the body. A malignant tumour discovered in his right leg would medically "result in" the amputation of that leg. (अंगच्छेदन)

◦ Correct: ... when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) amputation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fragmentation" — breaking into small pieces or parts; not a surgical treatment for a leg tumour.

• Option 3 "vasodilation" — the widening of blood vessels; unrelated to a tumour of the bone.

• Option 4 "implantation" — the insertion of tissue or a device into the body — the opposite of removal.

NOTE

• The passage refers to Terry Fox, the Canadian athlete whose right leg was amputated because of osteosarcoma; he then began the "Marathon of Hope" run across Canada to raise money for cancer research, and is commemorated by statues and by a Royal Canadian Mint coin.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

To mark the 25th anniversary of the run, (1) ______ Royal Canadian Mint unveiled a one-dollar commemorative circulation coin (2) ______ Monday on the campus of Simon Fraser University. Fox was (3) ______ undergraduate student and basketball player at SFU when a malignant tumour was discovered in his right leg in 1977. It resulted in (4) ______. A bronze statue of Fox, one of many such tributes across Canada, looks over the academic quadrangle of the university, just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) ______ was held.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. unveiling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unveiling" (noun) means a ceremony at which something new — a coin, a statue, a plaque — is formally shown to the public for the first time. (अनावरण)

• The passage itself says the Mint "unveiled" the coin, so the event held in the theatre was the unveiling.

◦ Correct: ... just a short stroll from the theatre where Monday's (5) unveiling was held.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "countervailing" — acting against something with equal force (as in "countervailing duty" in trade).

• Option 3 "reconciling" — bringing into agreement or making friendly again.

• Option 4 "veiling" — covering or concealing, the exact opposite of unveiling.

NOTE

• Word family: veil (a covering) → unveil (to remove the cover, to reveal) → unveiling (the ceremony of revealing). Similar pairs: cover/uncover, mask/unmask, cover-up/disclosure.
